sections.overview: Garra menoni is a small cyprinid described in 1984 from the Kunthi River in Kerala’s Silent Valley, India. The Catalog of Fishes confirms it as a valid species.
sections.identification: The type description notes a developed adhesive mental disc, two pairs of short barbels and 32–36 lateral-line scales.
sections.habitat: It inhabits freshwater mountain streams; the original specimens came from the forested Kunthi River in the Western Ghats.
sections.diet: The species accounts consulted do not report a diet or prey list specific to G. menoni.
sections.behavior: FishBase classifies it as benthopelagic, but detailed species-specific behavior is poorly documented.
sections.reproduction: The reviewed species-level sources do not describe spawning or parental care.
sections.ecology: The 1984 authors compared it with Garra mullya and G. lissorhynchus, distinguishing the new species by its morphology.
sections.conservation: FishBase displays Vulnerable (D2) from a 2010 assessment; this dated category should not be treated as a current reassessment.
